<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json be076dad28a0d35cefc7f76cd06950620cb8b81b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `44818e2e6df0671bf0b55140423ea2327e6e3943`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/contract.mdx, content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx, .changeset/24082-invite-role-cap-codes.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Inputs: card #24082 (body, claim `6226978922`, dev report `6227435484`); parent #23945 (body, comments `6217250590`, `6226340273`, `6226946317`); PR #24092 (body, five-file list, net diff `8a83cebc15..44818e2e6d`, where `8a83cebc15` is the merge-base with `origin/main`); the head's check-runs, read at 2026-10-17T01:03Z. Everything was read with `git show` / `git grep` at the sha and unauthenticated REST GETs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head (40 check-runs).** 34 are success, 5 are skipped by their path filters or opt-in (`Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`), and **1 is still in progress: `Test Core (3/6)`**, after a bounded wait. Its verdict is NOT read by this record. The other five Test Core shards are success. Tier S still needs every check green before the queue, so the seat reads 3/6 before landing. The gates this change rests on: `check:error-code-casing`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` and `check:error-code-provenance` (lint.yml `Lint · docs & code guards`, success); `check:docs` (`Type Check · source gates`, success); `check:api-surface` (`Type Check · consumer gates`, success); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` (ci.yml `Build Core`, success); `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, all success.

**The accept-set change is exactly three strings under `@objectstack/plugin-auth`.** The ledger hunk is +6/−0, all inside the `'@objectstack/plugin-auth'` array: a three-line block comment plus three rows, between `INVITE_EMAIL_FAILED` and `INVALID_REQUEST`. `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` feeds `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` and then `ErrorCode`, the union `ApiErrorSchema.code` validates against. That union gains exactly `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER`, `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` and `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED`. None of the three occurs anywhere at the merge-base (`git grep`: 0 hits), so none is a duplicate or a re-registration. No existing row is edited or moved, and no other owner key is touched. `STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS` and `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` are unchanged, and so is the standard catalog. The generated `contract.mdx` enum count moves from `+332 more` to `+335 more`: three, exactly.

**Each name against its producer.** The producer is `invitationRoleCapFailure` (`invitation-role-cap.ts` :159–:200). It has exactly three non-null returns, and every other exit returns `null`: :166 (no role), :167 (plain `member`) and :183 (the grant table admits the request). Its one caller is `beforeCreateInvitation` (`auth-manager.ts` :3415–:3423), which throws every non-null return as `new APIError('FORBIDDEN', { message })`. So the 403 that all three comments state is the status the producer answers today. It is also the status #23945 keeps when it stamps a `code` on that same throw.

| Code | Path | Reached when | Comment vs code |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` | :175–:181 | `orgRoleGrade(issuerRole) === GRADE_UNRESOLVED`: the issuer's role value parses to no role | matches (condition 3 below) |
| `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER` | :186–:192 | the grant table does not admit the request, and `orgRoleGrade(requested) > issuerGrade` | matches. Live-measured on #23945: a delegated issuer inviting as `admin` gets 403 |
| `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` | :194–:199 | the grant table does not admit the request, and the requested grade is at most the issuer's | matches. Live-measured on #23945: a delegated issuer inviting as `delegated_admin` gets 403 |

**The three are exactly the set: no fourth path, and none unreachable.** I read the paths against the grant table (`invitation-role-grant.ts` :69–:86). `owner` takes `[owner]`. `admin`, `delegated_admin` and any role the table does not list take `[owner, admin]`. `member` takes `'any'`. So an admin-grade issuer is refused only when it asks for `owner` without being an owner itself. That is grade 3 against grade 2, which lands on path :186. Path :194 is therefore reached only by an issuer below admin grade, as the `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` comment says. Its precondition (the requested grade is at most the issuer's, which is `member`) is the comment's "does not outrank theirs". Path :175 was not triggered live (#23945 says so). It is reachable in the code, though: `orgRoleGrade(null)` is 0, and `resolveMembershipRole` returns `null` from four exits (below). The hook's other refusals are the ADR-0090 D12 placement gate, not the role cap: the placement-runtime `FORBIDDEN` (:3429–:3436) and `assertIssuable` (:3439). The card scopes them out by its own text, and they hide no fourth cap path.

**Condition 3's wording holds.** `resolveMembershipRole` (`auth-manager.ts` :7612–:7633) returns `null` in four cases:
- missing keys (:7618);
- no engine (:7620);
- no usable row (:7629): none was found, or every row's `role` is empty or not a string (filtered at :7627–:7628);
- a lookup that threw (:7630–:7631).

The comment's main clause, "the issuer's `sys_member` role could not be established", covers all four. Its parenthetical, "no row, or the lookup did not answer", summarises them: "no row" is :7629, and "did not answer" is :7620 and :7631. It leaves out :7618, which an invitation that reaches the hook cannot practically produce: better-auth hands the hook a session user and an organization. The parenthetical is accurate for what it names and does not claim to be complete, so I accept it. "fail-closed" and "may confer nothing beyond `member`" match the file's own header (:40–:43) and path :175.

**Synonym gate (#8211).** None of the three is an HTTP reason phrase, so the first test in `standardSynonymOf` cannot match. Its second test needs every word of the code to appear in one standard code's name, but no `StandardErrorCode` member carries `INVITE`. (`errors.zod.ts` has no `INVITE`, `ISSUER` or `UNVERIFIED`.) So all three return `undefined`, no waiver is owed, and none was added. The names follow the header's registration rule: a domain prefix, inside the existing `INVITE_*` family, naming the condition and not the status.

**#16404, "door or no door".** The ledger is the published face, so registering the codes widens it. The rows land AHEAD of their producer: no `packages/**` source stamps them yet, so the provenance gate passes with nothing to check. The test file already records this split shape, for `FLOW_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, whose producer later landed. That makes it admissible; see ③ for the window before the producer lands.

**The added test is a real pin.** The case at `error-code-ledger.test.ts` :234–:244 checks three things for each code, by value: `ErrorCode.parse` accepts it, it is a member of `'@objectstack/plugin-auth'`, and `standardSynonymOf` returns `undefined`. It fails on a removal, a rename, a move to another owner, or a later standard code that would shadow one of them. Those cover the accept-set this PR changes, and #23945 will assert against the same strings. It cannot pin what a comment means, and it does not claim to. It is also not the "test pinned to a producerless code" the header warns about, because it pins registration, not emission.

**The regenerated docs are generated, with no hand edits.** Both pages carry the `AUTO-GENERATED — DO NOT EDIT` banner. Their hunks are the three bullets, each in sorted position, plus the `+335 more` count, and nothing else. `check:docs` (`build-docs.ts --check`) fails on any byte that differs from the generator's output, and it is success on this head. The docs-drift bot flagged four hand-written pages, but they name `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` only. None lists an `INVITE_*` code, so no docs update is owed.

### ② Semver level

**`minor` on `@objectstack/spec` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` matches what ships.** The PR body and the changeset both carry that line. `@objectstack/spec` is published (`publishConfig.access: public`). After this PR, `ErrorCode` and `ApiErrorSchema.code` accept three more strings, and nothing is removed or renamed, so the change is a widening. AGENTS.md says a `yes` takes at least `minor`. It is not `(narrowing)`, so it is not breaking and needs neither a migration note nor an ADR-0087 marker.

No other package owes a changeset: `plugin-auth` source is untouched, and the changeset says so ("still throws `FORBIDDEN` until #23945"). The changeset's three meaning lines agree with the ledger comments. Its condition-3 line says "could not be established" and does not mention a read fault, so the CHANGELOG text stays true whichever way question 1 is decided. `Check Changeset` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations**, each answered:
1. **A test case was added beyond the claim's file surface.** Accepted. It is one spec-lane file, the report declares it, it follows the file's own registered-ahead precedent, and it pins exactly the accept-set change.
2. **The gate battery was partly measured at `146a9615`.** Superseded: the check-runs on this head answer every family (see the gate verdicts in ①).
3. **`git fetch --unshallow origin main`.** A local environment act with no effect on the diff. Not a review matter.
4. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` were not measured locally.** Answered on this head. Both run in ci.yml `Build Core` (:2643 and :2667), which is success. The report and the PR body say they run in `Lint & Repo Gates`; that label is wrong, but nothing turns on it.

**open_questions[1]: should a thrown lookup answer 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of 403 `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED`?**

**Ruled: this card is right to register one code now and leave the split to #23945. Covering a read fault in the comment is not a wrong contract sentence that must change before landing.** Four reasons:
- **The code string is the contract, and it is the same under both options.** What #16404 makes the published face is the string a consumer's `switch (e.code)` pins. That string, and the accept-set of `ErrorCode`, are identical under option A and option B. Under B, the thrown lookup moves to `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, a standard code that already exists. `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` keeps a meaning (no usable row). No code is added or removed, and narrowing the comment later is not a Clause-② event. Registering now closes off neither option.
- **The read-fault clause is true of today's producer.** The `catch { return null; }` at :7630–:7631 feeds path :175. A comment written to option B's meaning would describe a producer that does not exist. It would also pre-decide a `plugin-auth` question (what `resolveMembershipRole` returns), and the claim bars this card from that source ("⛔ No `plugin-auth` source").
- **The clause never reaches consumers as wire text.** The reference pages carry the bare names only, and the CHANGELOG line says only "could not be established".
- **The #21941 rule is the producer's to apply.** `auth-manager.ts` :1328–:1330 says a read that could not answer "is not a verdict … so it must not wear the refusal's words". That rule is why the dev's lean toward option B is sound, and also why the decision belongs on #23945.

What this ruling hands to #23945 (escalated, not blocking):
- **(a) Decide.** #23945 decides option A or option B on the record.
- **(b) Narrow the comment if B.** If it picks B, the same landing removes "or the lookup did not answer" from the `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` comment. That is a `packages/spec` path, so either #23945's claim declares it as a spec-lane surface, or a spec card is owed. Otherwise the ledger keeps describing a behaviour the producer no longer has.
- **(c) Place "no engine" if B.** #23945 also says where the no-engine exit (:7620) goes. The slug guard's rule for a missing engine, that the guard does not apply (:3507–:3511), cannot carry over to a security cap.
- **(d) Re-measure path :175 if B.** #23945 measures that path :175 still has a reachable input. If better-auth refuses a non-member before `beforeCreateInvitation` runs, what remains is a race or a row with no role. This review did not measure that ordering: better-auth is not installed in the read tree, and nothing was installed.

**open_questions[2], the names: A, as landed.** Each name states its condition, carries the domain prefix the header asks for, sits in the existing `INVITE_*` family, and clears the synonym gate with no waiver. They are also the exact strings #23945 will assert by value. There is no ground to rename.

**Window before the producer lands (escalated to the seat).** Until #23945 stamps these codes, the three rows are what the header's "Retiring a code" section describes: "a registered-but-unemittable row stays green forever". No gate fails on that. Admission checks casing, duplication and shadowing, and the provenance gate only checks that a code which is stamped is also registered, not the reverse. This is acceptable as the recorded split shape. When this PR lands, #23945 (`pm:blocked` on this card) should be released. If #23945 is abandoned, these rows come out.

**VERDICT: PASS**
